hook: Badrinarayanan helped write one of computer vision's most-cited deep learning papers, SegNet, before moving into frontier AI research at DeepMind, and now leads AI development at Wayve, applying end-to-end learned driving models rather than the hand-coded rule systems most autonomous vehicle companies rely on.
name: Vijay Badrinarayanan

quote.text: The future of autonomous driving is not thousands of hand-coded rules, it's a single AI system that learns to drive the way humans do, from experience.
quote.context: A recurring theme in Badrinarayanan's public remarks on Wayve's end-to-end learning approach

moniker: Computer Vision Researcher Behind SegNet and Wayve's Self-Driving AI

primary.name: SegNet: A Deep Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Architecture for Image Segmentation, Badrinarayanan, Kendall, Cipolla, IEEE TPAMI (2017)
Vijay Badrinarayanan, Wayve leadership team, official site

timeline.event: Publishes SegNet with collaborators at Cambridge
timeline.impact: Introduces a widely adopted segmentation architecture

timeline.event: Joins DeepMind as a research scientist
Joins Wayve as VP of AI
timeline.impact: Leads end-to-end AI development for autonomous driving

quick_facts: Co-author of SegNet, a foundational deep learning architecture for image segmentation
VP of AI at Wayve, a UK-based autonomous driving company
Previously a research scientist on DeepMind's core research team
PhD from the University of Cambridge in computer vision

achievements.title: Co-authoring SegNet (2015)
achievements.impact: Introduced an encoder-decoder deep learning architecture for pixel-wise image segmentation that became a standard reference architecture across computer vision research and industry applications.

achievements.title: Research scientist, DeepMind
achievements.impact: Contributed to frontier deep learning research at one of the field's leading labs.

achievements.title: VP of AI, Wayve
achievements.impact: Leads development of Wayve's end-to-end learned driving models, an approach that trains a single AI system to drive directly from sensor input rather than composing separate hand-engineered modules.

achievements.title: PhD research in Bayesian computer vision, University of Cambridge
achievements.impact: Built the academic foundation underlying his later deep learning segmentation and perception work.
